overview: 50 official Group 1 Qs (2008–2024) spread over agriculture, irrigation, farm credit, industrial policy, reforms, energy, BoP and WTO. 2008–2019 were mostly one-liners (who sponsors, which year, which body); 2023–24 moved to statement-based, A-R and match items on schemes, indices and WTO boxes. Heaviest: LPG reforms and 1991 crisis (11 Qs) and irrigation/water (8 Qs).

possibility.angle: Features of Indian agriculture – weather dependence
possibility.what_they_ask: A-R linking monsoon uncertainty to fluctuating agriculture and NI growth
project → state/district, traditional harvesting system → region, PMKSY components, irrigated vs rainfed share, high groundwater-use states and basins
natural targets judging by neighbouring leaves: HYV crops of the Green Revolution, fertiliser subsidy/NBS, soil health card, seed and input schemes with launch years

possibility.angle: Agricultural strategy and policy – missions, insurance, markets, indices
possibility.what_they_ask: which mission matches an aim (NMSA – climate), scheme slogans (PMFBY), e-NAM and APLM Act aims, AOI publisher and formula
AP committee chairmen (crop holiday – Mohan Kanda), main cause of farmer suicides (NCRB ADSI)
who formulated KCC, who sponsors RRBs, where LDBs belong, credit duration bands
which body recommends MSP (CACP) vs decides vs procures
PDS coverage–leakage logic; natural targets: NFSA 2013 entitlements, ONORC
which railway unit makes what and where
which IPR is the 'Economic Constitution', what NIP 1991 allowed (51% FDI in high-priority industries)

possibility.angle: Make in India and ease of doing business
possibility.what_they_ask: state ranking order in an EoDB index (AP first)
eligibility details (greenfield only, non-individual allowed), loan mechanics (OD vs cash credit), SISFS, Fund of Funds, MAARG
year of SEZ policy (2000) vs Act (2005) vs rules (2006); natural targets: corridor names and end-points
UDAY demand-side measure, HELP revenue-sharing model, coal washing and merit-order dispatch
the crisis behind 1991, its immediate cause, how it was tided over, which sector stayed unreformed, which measure is not a reform, MNC effects
BoP classification (ADR/GDR = portfolio), debit vs credit entries, CAD drivers, LPI rank
WTO DG at the time, Green/Blue/Amber box rules, Bali peace clause, AMS

traps.trap: Swaps the role an institution plays in a chain (recommends / sponsors / formulates)
traps.spot: One-liner naming several banks or bodies for a scheme or rural bank
traps.fix: RRB sponsor = commercial bank; KCC formulated by NABARD; MSP recommended by CACP, decided by CCEA
traps.pyq: 'Regional Rural Bank [...] sponsored by' → Scheduled Commercial Bank [group1-prelims-2010#90]; KCC → NABARD [group1-prelims-2008#96]; MSP → CACP [group1-prelims-2010#81]

traps.trap: Reverses what a WTO box allows
traps.spot: 'prohibits', 'must not exceed', 'is not to be placed' in box statements
traps.fix: Green = decoupled payments allowed; Blue = production-limiting support allowed; peace clause shields breach of the 10% limit
traps.pyq: Statements I, II, IV false → only III [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#82]

traps.trap: Reverses the aim of a reform law
traps.spot: A-R where R states the law's 'focus'
traps.fix: APLM Act 2017 aims at a single state market and inter-mandi trade; intra-mandi dominance is the gap, not the aim

traps.trap: Widens or narrows a scheme's coverage
traps.spot: 'brownfield along with greenfield', 'exclusive platform for AI'
traps.fix: Stand-Up India = greenfield only; MAARG = sector-agnostic mentorship
traps.pyq: Stand-Up I false [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#75]; MAARG II false [group1-prelims-2024-paper1#80]

traps.trap: Substitutes the publisher of an index
traps.fix: AOI is FAO (SDG 2.a.1), not IFPRI; LPI is World Bank
traps.pyq: AOI statement I false → II and III [group1-prelims-2023-paper2#113]

traps.trap: Mixes immediate and structural causes of 1991
traps.spot: Options list political instability, non-oil imports, Soviet trade, oil imports
traps.fix: Immediate trigger = Gulf war oil price spike; base = BoP/fiscal crisis; rescue = IMF loan with gold pledged
traps.pyq: → oil and petroleum imports [group1-prelims-2017-paper1#33]; → IMF loan by pledging gold [group1-prelims-2017-paper1#34]

traps.trap: Inserts a non-component into a scheme's component list
traps.spot: Negative 'not a component of' with one large separate plan
traps.fix: PMKSY = AIBP + Har Khet ko Pani + Per Drop More Crop + watershed; National Water Grid is separate

traps.trap: Swaps regions in water-harvesting and project matches
traps.spot: Match list of local names or dam projects with states
traps.fix: Zing–Ladakh, Zabo–Nagaland, Johad–Rajasthan, Phad–Maharashtra, Eri/Yeri–TN, Korambu–Kerala; Renukaji–HP, Lakhwar–Uttarakhand, Parwan–Rajasthan, Ken-Betwa–MP/UP
traps.pyq: A-III, B-V, C-II, D-IV, E-I [group1-prelims-2017-paper1#51]; IV III II I [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#112]

techniques.name: Odd-one-out by direction of policy
techniques.how: In 'not a reform' or 'out of place' items, mark each option as loosening (+) or tightening (–) control, or as a good vs bad effect. The option with the opposite sign is the answer.
techniques.example: SEZs, less SSI reservation [...] and removing entry barriers all deregulate; 'greater rigour in labour laws' tightens → option 2 [group1-prelims-2010-reexam#23]; MNC list: export obligations is the only positive [group1-prelims-2010-reexam#27]

techniques.name: Shares must add up
techniques.how: When a statement gives a share (irrigated %, rainfed %), check it against its complement in another option.
techniques.example: '55% of NCA rainfed' and '60% irrigated' cannot both hold; rainfed ~50–55% is true, so the 60% claim is incorrect [group1-prelims-2019-paper1#67]

techniques.name: Supply vs demand side sort
techniques.how: Classify each option by where it acts: generation/fuel (supply), network losses (operational), funding (financial), consumer use (demand).
techniques.example: Coal swapping supply, cheap funds financial, T&D loss operational → LED bulbs is demand side [group1-prelims-2017-paper1#14]

techniques.name: Debit = money goes out
techniques.how: For any BoP entry, ask whether foreign exchange leaves (debit) or arrives (credit), regardless of the label.
techniques.example: Exports and gifts received bring money in; a gift to foreigners sends it out → debit [group1-prelims-2010-reexam#21]

techniques.name: Contract model recall
techniques.how: Match each hydrocarbon or licensing regime to its revenue model before reading options.
techniques.example: NELP = production sharing; HELP = biddable revenue sharing → option 2 [group1-prelims-2017-paper1#138]

techniques.name: Anchor pair in match lists
techniques.how: Fix the most distinctive pair (Ken-Betwa = MP/UP, Zabo = Nagaland), then check which codes keep it; usually one survives.
techniques.example: d-I leaves options 2 and 4; Renukaji = HP (b-III) keeps only 'IV III II I' [group1-prelims-2023-paper1#112]

techniques.name: Sector status check for post-1991 reforms
techniques.how: List sectors opened after 1991 (aviation, telecom, banking, insurance) and those kept with the state (railways, atomic energy).

confusions.remember: Recommend – decide – procure: CACP – CCEA – FCI
Land development banks are the long-term cooperative arm
Policy, then Act, then rules; Kandla EPZ 1965
NELP shares production after cost recovery; HELP shares revenue, open acreage
Green decoupled, allowed; Blue production-limiting, allowed; Amber trade-distorting, capped
Stand-Up = bank loan ₹10 lakh–1 cr to SC/ST/women, greenfield; Startup = recognition, SISFS, Fund of Funds (SIDBI)
Farmers' welfare commission vs crop holiday committee
Control and lasting interest vs tradable securities
Dunkel Draft belongs to GATT's Uruguay Round

anchors: 1991 BoP crisis: oil price spike trigger, gold pledged, IMF loan, then LPG reforms
NIP 1991: automatic 51% FDI in 34 high-priority industries
KCC 1998, formulated by NABARD (R.V. Gupta Committee)
PMKSY (2015): AIBP, Har Khet ko Pani, Per Drop More Crop, watershed
e-NAM / APLM Act 2017: one unified market, barrier-free inter-mandi trade
Stand-Up India: ₹10 lakh–₹1 crore, greenfield, OD up to ₹10 lakh, CGFSIL cover
AOI = FAO, SDG indicator 2.a.1: agriculture share of govt spending ÷ agriculture share of GDP
HELP = revenue sharing; UDAY demand side = LED bulbs, efficient pumps
High groundwater use: Punjab, Haryana, Rajasthan, TN; low: Odisha
Jurala project – Mahabubnagar, on the Krishna
checklist: Which role is asked – recommends, sponsors, formulates, regulates or procures?
For a scheme statement: is the coverage widened or narrowed (greenfield, exclusive, all)?
For WTO/law statements: is the stated aim the real aim or its reverse?
In odd-one-out lists, mark each option's direction (+/–) and pick the one with the other sign
For years: policy, Act or rules – which one does the stem ask?
For indices: check publisher and edition before the rank or formula
For 1991 items: immediate trigger, structural cause or rescue measure?
